entries.title: Note arm-on-release + armed-line-is-a-name on the behaviors link-drop tile
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. TWO fixes to the dropped-link gesture, both found by reproduction after 'nothing is added on completing'. (1) ARM ON RELEASE: reading the open-graph card takes ~1.2s measured, and until it landed the command line stayed empty and the chevron cold — Enter in that window created NOTHING and the drop showed no sign of having registered. The chevron now arms on release holding just the URL (measured t=0), and the title + picture fill the SAME slot when they arrive, matched by an armId; commit or dismiss RETIRES the id so a late card cannot raise a chevron over a finished gesture. Committing inside the window yields a tile with the link and no picture — the image is optional, as designed. (2) AN ARMED LINE IS A NAME: with something armed, a non-slash line goes straight to create instead of through tag extraction and the behaviour table. A video titles itself, and those titles carry operators — a leading '~' is remove-cell, so the create never happened at all; '&', '#' and '?' truncated 'Q&A #5 what?! + more' to 'qa'. Now: 'tilde-title', 'qa-5-what-more', 'next-level'. Cost: create-time ':tag' while armed lands in the name instead of persisting a tag. Slash commands still run while armed (verified /help).

entries.title: Note the URL-derived name + the Link field following the service
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. TWO further fixes on the dropped-link gesture. (1) A DROP ALWAYS YIELDS A NAME: the command line is seeded from the URL itself on release (youtube <id>, or the publisher's slug / host for other links — link-name.ts, defaultNameForLink), and the open-graph title REPLACES that seed when it arrives, but only while the line is still the one we seeded. Before this, any drop whose card could not be read — a platform that publishes none, or a browser whose tracking protection blocks youtube.com — left an armed chevron over an empty line and an Enter that did nothing. Verified with youtube.com/ytimg.com fetches force-rejected: line reads 'youtube aircAruvnKk' and the create works. (2) THE EDITOR'S LINK FIELD FOLLOWS THE SERVICE: linkValue was a plain field filled ONLY at open, so a link dropped onto an ALREADY-OPEN editor never appeared — and save() wrote that stale field straight back, ERASING the dropped link. It is now a signal refreshed from the service on every change (never while that input has focus). Verified: field flips to the dropped URL, save persists it across a reopen.

entries.title: Note the three ways a link drop used to do nothing at all
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. THREE fixes so a dropped link can never silently do nothing. (1) DRAGOVER CLAIMS ANYTHING CARRYING A LINK: it used to refuse when the source ADVERTISED the 'Files' type, which a dragged browser TAB and links out of native apps do while delivering no file at all — no preventDefault meant the drop event was never delivered and the whole gesture vanished. Real files are still handed to ImageDropDrone, decided at drop by dataTransfer.files.length, which is the only place it is knowable. (2) NO IN-FLIGHT GUARD: #busy was held across every await of the route (safety check, card read, picture fetch), so a second drop within those seconds was discarded without a trace, and any route that never settled wedged the gesture PERMANENTLY. Each drop is its own gesture now, carrying its own armId; per-cell writes already serialise on their own lock. (3) ARM BEFORE THE SAFETY CHECK: the arm sat behind an LLM safety call whose endpoint is loopback (127.0.0.1:4220) and can be absent or behind a Local Network Access prompt. The chevron now lights on release and a denied link RETRACTS it via command:disarm-resource.

entries.title: Note the real-drag harness on the behaviors link-drop tile
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. scripts/verify-link-drop.cjs drives a REAL native drag with Playwright (trusted CDP input, the browser's own DataTransfer) and asserts the five steps: drop delivered / open-graph card read / command line named by the title / tile carries the dropped URL / picture from the og image. Two modes: default drops on empty canvas and presses Enter; --tile drops on an existing tile (link + picture land there, command line deliberately untouched). Synthetic new DragEvent() cannot stand in for this — it never exercises the browser's DataTransfer and cannot show whether dragover ACCEPTED the drag, which is exactly where the gesture was being lost.

entries.title: Note create-on-drop, deadlines, and the ONE-TAB packed-store trap on the link-drop tile
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. (1) DROPPING ON EMPTY SPACE IS THE CREATION: the drop commits itself (command:commit-armed) instead of waiting for an Enter nobody asked to press; the tile is pinned to the first slot (props index 0, atTop through arm-resource → ResourceAttachDrone) and the title stays in the line naming what landed. Dropping on an EXISTING tile still only pastes the link, and now asks first (requestConfirm) before replacing a link that tile already had. (2) DEADLINES ON EVERY NETWORK STEP (deadline.ts): card read 3.5s, picture 5s, safety verdict 5s, each aborting what it abandons. A hung request is worse than a failed one — it parked the whole drop with no title, no picture and no tile. (3) THE PICTURE IS BEST-EFFORT IN THE STORE TOO: armImageBlob throwing used to take the link with it; it now degrades to the bare arm. (4) THE TRAP THAT COST A DAY: the packed store admits ONE WRITER — a second tab on the same origin comes up with opfsAvailable false and putResource throwing 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading getFileHandle)'. Every symptom of a dead drop follows. Console says it plainly: '[packed-store] unavailable — held by another tab'. NEVER open a second tab (in-app browser pane, MCP tab, Playwright against the same profile) on a hive someone is using; Playwright with its own profile is safe. Harness: scripts/verify-link-drop.cjs.

entries.title: Note the open-graph verification popup on the link-drop tile

Two modes: 'verify' REPORTS and never gates the gesture (one OK button; this is what a drop shows today, as a test aid), 'confirm' asks and can cancel, and names the link it would replace. entries.title: Note the root-context follow on the Beehaviors tile
entries.note: The Beehaviors window follows navigation all the way to the ROOT: backing out to / no longer leaves the panel on the previous tile's group — the hive itself becomes the subject. THE ROOT CONTEXT IS THE HOME PAGE: the group names itself from the root layer's own name (whatever is active at /), falling back to 'hypercomb' only when the layer carries none; when named hive roots land, this same spot resolves the ACTIVE hive's name. Root rows read the root layer's decorations authoritatively (the label-keyed hot index is skipped at root so a tile sharing the display name can't leak kinds in), the root is never a peer-branch offer, and ADD/REMOVE work at the root: empty segments WITH a named cell is the hive-root group, a real write target on the root layer.

entries.title: Note the landing ring for link drags on the link-drop tile
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. A link drag now ANNOUNCES itself (drop:dragging active on the first dragover, cleared on drop, dragend, and a dragleave that exits the window). Before this the ring machinery was dormant for links — only ImageDropDrone announced — so the overlay went on HOVER-highlighting whichever tile the pointer passed, a tile the drop had nothing to do with. drop:dragging now carries atTop, and DropLandingDrone rings slot 0 instead of the tail of the spiral when set, because a dropped link mints its tile at the TOP; the flag is absent for every other drag, so their behaviour is unchanged. Restores what commit f29cd5a50 (wip, 2026-04-12) removed when it replaced create-on-drop with command-line arming.

entries.title: Note the roster-flip refresh on the Beehaviors tile
entries.note: One switch, one meaning — and one truth across both views: flipping a behavior on the GLOBAL roster now re-marks the per-tile view immediately. The tile group's rows carry their dormant/global-off marks from group-open time, so leaving the store re-requests the group (closeStore refresh) and any enablement change (roster switch, wake-here, publisher-withheld record) refreshes an open tile group in place. Dormant means gone: an attached behavior turned off globally disappears from the tile view AND stops acting on the canvas (view.bee falls back to hexagons, toggles and offers withdraw); its decorations stay on the tile untouched, so re-enabling globally brings everything straight back.

entries.title: Global fit reconciles against the surface + chrome, not just window resize
entries.note: Fix: the global fit switch refit was bound only to window 'resize'. When the DRAWING SURFACE changed with no window resize (a panel reserving a column, the shell re-laying out) or when only the CHROME moved (header grows a row as a drop arms the command line, controls rail docks/undocks), nothing refit — the page kept the scale/position computed for the previous safe area, leaving content small and pushed into a corner. pixi-host already reconciled the CANVAS for this reason (resyncToHost) but only recentres the stage, so the renderer reported the new surface while the fit kept the old framing. Now a 250ms signature reconciler samples canvas box + --hc-controls-left/right + header bottom and refits only on change. Owed: a note on the fit-switch tile under behaviors describing the two non-window triggers, so the mark explains why the fit follows chrome. Manual because note-add is additive and would land twice.

entries.title: Global fit: back-nav paints land BEFORE the navigate that arms them
entries.note: Fix: arrived() was gated purely on an arm set by the window 'navigate' event. Verified event order — forward nav: navigate -> cell-count (fit runs). BACK nav (MovementService.back / history.back): cell-count, cell-count, THEN navigate. Every paint at the destination ran unarmed and bailed, so the page was NEVER refit on the way back; it kept whatever stale snapshot the viewport store held (auto-fits never persist, so that snapshot can be from any earlier moment) — the 'it shrinks when I click back' report. Now arrived() also treats an unsettled page key as an arrival (#lastSettledPageKey), so the fit is independent of event ORDER; add/remove stillness is preserved because those paint the same key already settled. Owed: a note on the fit-switch tile under behaviors recording that arrival is a LOCATION change, not an event, and why back-nav inverts the order.

entries.title: Viewport source splits GESTURE from PERSIST — 'auto-persist' added, ratchet frozen
entries.note: Sweep after the back-click fix. Root cause class: automatic code borrowing a user-gesture path. (1) source 'user' meant BOTH 'persist this' and 'the participant asked' — the latter announces viewport:fit, which the control bar uses to DISCARD a page's hand framing. Three automatic callers claimed 'user' purely to persist (auto-fit-first-add, show-cell first-visit fit, and the comments all said 'so it STICKS'): a first-tile add or first-visit render silently stripped a hand framing and the page re-fitted forever after. Added ViewportSource 'auto-persist' = persists (even through suspend) but never announces; migrated the two truly automatic callers; sequence-cycle stays 'user' (it follows an "a" keypress). (2) Mirror image: zoomByFactor/zoomToScale/animateToScale unconditionally emitted viewport:manual, which MARKS a page hand-framed — so the tutorial zoom LESSON permanently excluded whatever page it ran on from global fit. Added a source param defaulting to 'user'; tutorial passes 'auto'. Also fixed controls-bar passing an undeclared third arg 'controls-bar' that would now read as a source and demote the magnifier buttons. (3) pixi-host now emits render:surface-resized from resyncToHost — the missing 'the canvas changed size without a window resize' signal; center-slot-tracker consumed it (its scores were ranking slots against a dead viewport after a panel opened). Guard: doctrine.spec.ts ratchet 'viewport source user means a GESTURE' with a 4-entry allowlist, verified to FAIL when the regression is reintroduced. Owed: a note on the fit-switch tile recording the two-question source model (persist vs gesture) and why marks/mode changes must never ride a gesture path.

entries.title: Note the hyperlink-vs-image drop arbitration on the link-drop tile
entries.note: MANUAL — note-add is additive. THE bug behind 'no text, no link, file icon at the top': dragging a video off the YouTube page packages an IMAGE FILE and the URL in one drag. ImageDropDrone registered first and claimed any drop with files, so the gesture minted a mute picture tile — no name, no link — and LinkDropWorker never saw it (its own guard bailed on files.length). Found by reading the participant's replayed bus values: command:arm-resource with largeSig true, url null, name null = the image path's signature. Arbitration is now BY CONTENT and order-independent, decided identically on both sides via extractDroppedUrl (link-drop-destination.ts): a drop carrying a URL that is NOT itself an image is a HYPERLINK — the link path claims it and the dragged file becomes the tile's picture (beats fetching); no URL, or a URL that IS the image (a bare drag), stays with the image path. Harness gained --thumb: a real drag of , the exact YouTube shape — 8/8.

entries.title: Mirror: the root shows the marked home's data, address stays /
entries.note: SHIPPED. Supersedes the home-is-the-root entry (that one redirected the URL; this one does not). hypercomb-shared/core/home-root.ts exports homeSubstituted(address) + showHiveRoot(); Lineage.followLocation — the ONE place an address becomes a location — substitutes an empty address for the marked home's segments, so sigbag/currentLayer/explorerDir/render all resolve to home while the URL and breadcrumb stay at the root. Walking in materializes the real address (/<home>/<child>); showHiveRoot() suspends the substitution while standing deliberately on the bare root and lapses on walking away. Mark is set per-row in the Portals toolwindow (one slot); Ctrl+click Home lists recent portals for travel only. Tiles for home-root.ts, lineage.ts followLocation, recent-portals.store.ts, aggregate-index.component.*, controls-bar.component.*. Notes on the why: a shortcut is a second way to reach a place, a home changes what the first way MEANS — which is why nothing is spelled out in the address.

entries.title: Swarm byte path — a shared tile brings its pictures, R2 hosts them
entries.note: No mirror pass run (no live bridge). Owed under behaviors/swarm: (1) a part tile for the BYTE PATH with a note stating the rule — the swarm carries SIGNATURES, never bytes; layers have a mesh fallback, resources do NOT, so a picture is only ever fetched from a host; (2) a note on the join card that joining PROVISIONS a byte target (own host wins, else the public content endpoint's 100MB/90d auto-grant) and that joining is the consent gesture for staging bytes; (3) a part tile for the AVAILABILITY GATE — announce only what a host has receipted, held tiles announce when receipts land, hc:swarm:ungated is the explicit dev-loop escape. Ties to the standing 'bytes before broadcast' doctrine. Files: hypercomb-essentials/src/diamondcoreprocessor.com/sharing/host-sync.service.ts (ensureSwarmTarget), sharing/swarm.drone.ts (gate + mesh:public-changed), sharing/content-broker.drone.ts (#resolveRemote layer-only fallback).
